about: The check-in, wallet and gate screens' wording. render_airline.py checks every string under traveler as it checks the pages: no rule, theorem or criterion, no requirement ID, no typed amount. Strings under lean show only with the Lean model. Under lean, requirements must name requirements the model has, open must name criteria that are still open, and element must name an identifier of the model. Results are computed; this file holds only the words for each result.

traveler.note: Verified Airline is a fictional airline. This is a proof of concept, not affiliated with IATA. The traveler, the flight and the credentials are specimens.

MatchReading: When a refusal lands: a traveler learns at the gate today. The same check at check-in would warn them with time to fix it.
Who carries each error: a wrong refusal sends a traveler to an agent, and a wrong acceptance boards someone on another traveler's pass.
What the gate receives: requiring both credentials sends the name and the portrait to the gate. The wallet's sheet lists them before it shares.
No face step: this demo has no camera, so the portrait goes unused here. A touchpoint would match a face against it.
ValidityReading.departure: After a refusal: this demo cannot reissue a boarding pass, so a traveler on a delayed flight ends at an agent.
ValidityReading.soonAfter: A long window leaves a boarding pass valid after the journey, and nothing in the guide ends it sooner.
ExpiryReading.validAtEnd: Under one setting, a boarding pass set to end at departure is refused at the moment of departure.
PhotoidReading.portraitRequired: A photoid with no face image gives a touchpoint nothing to match.
PhotoidReading.passportRequired: Under the looser setting a photoid from another document is accepted, and nothing the reader must receive says so.
PhotoidValidityReading: Under the looser setting a photoid stays valid after its passport expires.
BoardingPassReading.unlistedDataAllowed: Under the looser setting a reader cannot tell what a boarding pass holds from the guide alone.
BoardingPassReading.repeatedNamesRefused: Under the looser setting a boarding pass with two strings is accepted, and the reader receives one of them.
PairReading.content: Comparing names here has the errors the matching switch shows for credentials alone. A traveler whose names are written differently is refused.
PairReading.sameDeviceKey: Requiring one device key refuses a traveler who holds a credential on a second device, and it accepts two travelers sharing one phone.
ConsentReading: This demo offers all or nothing. Under one setting a traveler who declines the portrait still sends the rest, and under the other the wallet sends nothing of that credential.
